name: Public Health Professional
description: ⚠⚠⚠ The job most students picture when they say public health is the smallest one in the federal data. Epidemiologists: 12,300 employed in the whole country, about 800 openings a year, and entry is effectively 100% graduate. The jobs are in health education (71,800, $64,070) and community health work (65,100, $51,850, high-school entry). ⚠⚠ Florida's own numbers say the same thing from the other side — 579 master's degrees against 560 bachelor's, at just 8 institutions, every one a university.
credentialNote: ⚠⚠⚠ THE CREDENTIAL IS COUNTABLE, AND IT IS NOT THE MAJOR. NCHEC's CHES — Certified Health Education Specialist — takes a bachelor's, master's or doctoral degree from an accredited institution, PLUS either a transcript showing a major in health education OR at least 25 SEMESTER CREDITS of coursework, with a grade of C or better, addressing the Nine Areas of Responsibility. ⚠⚠ The distribution is specified: a minimum of 12 credits from process courses, a maximum of 9 from topic-focused courses, and a maximum of 6 from other courses — so you cannot reach it by stacking topic electives. ⚠⚠⚠ That makes this one of the few choice paths where the credential can be planned from the first term with a calculator rather than a hope. Pull the Nine Areas from NCHEC, map them onto your catalogue, and count. ⚠ MCHES is the master's-level version, adding academic preparation at master's level and professional experience. ⚠ Nothing here is licensed by Florida — not health education specialists, not community health workers, not epidemiologists. For graduate study the accreditor that matters is CEPH, the Council on Education for Public Health; verify a programme's status with CEPH itself. ⚠⚠ And note the contrast with health care administration, the neighbouring path: there, Florida STATUTE rewards the MAJOR (s. 468.1695 halves a licensure internship for it). Here the credential rewards the COURSEWORK and ignores the major entirely. Two adjacent health fields, opposite answers to the same question.
bodyHtml:
⚠⚠⚠ The three jobs, and the famous one is the smallest

RoleSOC2025 medianEmployedOpenings/yrGrowth 2024–34Entry
Health education specialist21-1091$64,07071,8007,900faster than average (5–6%)bachelor's
Community health worker21-1094$51,85065,1007,800✅ much faster (7%+)⚠ high school
⚠⚠ Epidemiologist19-1041$87,220⚠⚠ 12,300⚠⚠⚠ 800✅ much faster (7%+)⚠ 67% master's, 22% post-doc, 11% doctorate

⚠⚠⚠ Read the epidemiologist row carefully before choosing this field for that reason. Twelve thousand three hundred people hold the job in the entire United States, and about eight hundred positions open a year. It pays well, it is growing fast, and there is almost none of it — and every route in requires a graduate degree.

⚠⚠ That is not an argument against public health. It is an argument for knowing which job you are aiming at. Health education and community health work together employ 137,000 people and open about 15,700 positions a year — nearly twenty times the epidemiology figure.

⚠⚠ O*NET and BLS disagree about how you get in, and it is worth knowing

SourceEntry education for health education specialists
BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook✅ bachelor's degree
⚠ O*NET respondent survey⚠ 62% said associate degree, 31% bachelor's

⚠ They do not agree, so this page quotes both. BLS reports the typical entry level; O*NET reports what its respondents said their own job required, and those are different questions. The credential sides with BLS — CHES requires a bachelor's at minimum — so plan on the degree and treat the O*NET figure as evidence that some employers hire below it.

⚠ The two sources also use different projection decades: BLS projects 6% growth and about 6,900 annual openings for 2025–35; O*NET reports 5–6% and 7,900 for 2024–34. Same picture, different vintage.

⚠⚠⚠ Florida says “master's field” twice, in two independent datasets

First, the degrees awarded (IPEDS, general public health, 2023):

LevelCredentials
⚠⚠ Master's⚠⚠ 579
Bachelor's560
Research doctorate44

⚠⚠⚠ The master's outnumbers the bachelor's — which happens in no other programme on this site.

Second, the courses. Of the 18 PHC courses carried by four or more Florida public institutions, 14 are graduate. Only three undergraduate PHC numbers reach four carriers at all.

⚠⚠ So treat the MPH as the normal terminal credential and the bachelor's as the first half, and budget for it from the start rather than discovering it in your final year.

⚠⚠ The undergraduate subject is numbered HSC, not PHC

A student who searches the PHC prefix finds a graduate catalogue and reasonably concludes there is no undergraduate route. There is — it is filed under HSC:

CourseFL institutions
HSC4500 Epidemiology9 — ⚠ five of them STATE COLLEGES
HSC4730 Public Health Research7
HSC3032 Foundations of Public Health5
HSC3661 Communication Theory and Practice for Health5
PHC2100 Introduction to Public Health5

⚠ Search both prefixes, and register by number.

⚠⚠⚠ Access: the opposite of the degree next door

Public healthHealth care administration
FL public institutions⚠ 824
Sector⚠⚠ all universities✅ 20 state colleges carry upper division
Median of the target job$64,070$123,860

⚠⚠ These two subjects overlap considerably at the policy end and are not equally reachable. If staying at a state college matters — and for a working adult it usually does — that is a real constraint and it should be part of the decision, not a discovery.

⚠⚠ The credential is 25 credits, and you can count them now

CHES does not require a health education major. It requires a bachelor's plus 25 semester credits addressing NCHEC's Nine Areas of Responsibility, at C or better, distributed as:

  • at least 12 credits from process courses — assessment, planning, implementation, evaluation, advocacy, communication;
  • at most 9 credits from topic-focused courses;
  • at most 6 credits from other courses.

⚠⚠⚠ The ceiling on topic courses is the part that catches people. Nutrition, substance use, sexual health and chronic disease are the interesting courses and they are the capped ones. You must deliberately take the programme-planning and evaluation coursework, and it is the part nobody chooses for fun.

⚠ Do this in your first term: get the Nine Areas from NCHEC, map your catalogue onto them, and count. It is a spreadsheet, and on a path where most advice is vague, it is a number.

Necessary skills

  • Programme planning and evaluation as a formal discipline — needs assessment, logic models, process and outcome measures. This is the professional core and the capped-credit rule exists to protect it.
  • Statistics you can actually use. Rates, risk, confounding, and why a difference might not be one.
  • Writing for a grant reviewer and for a county commission — two audiences, both unforgiving, and most public health work is funded by the first and answerable to the second.
  • Working with communities that have been surveyed before and seen nothing change. Credibility is the scarce resource.
  • Plain-language health communication, including to people who distrust the source.
  • Tolerance for slow, political, underfunded work. The wins are real and they are measured in years.

Advice

⚠⚠⚠ Decide early whether you are aiming at epidemiology. If you are, plan the master's or doctorate from the beginning, load up on statistics and quantitative methods, and accept that you are competing for about 800 openings a year nationally. If you are not, say so — and aim at health education or community health, where the jobs are.

⚠⚠ Count your CHES credits from term one. Twenty-five, at least twelve of them process courses, maximum nine topic. It is the single most concrete thing you can do on this path.

⚠ Budget for the MPH. In Florida the master's outnumbers the bachelor's in this field; treat it as the norm and check the programme's CEPH status with CEPH.

⚠ Check availability before you commit. Eight institutions, all universities. If you need a state college, look hard at health care administration or health information management instead — both overlap and both are far more widely taught.

And get into a health department, a federally qualified health centre or a community organisation early, in any capacity. This is a field where a graduate with two years of real community work beats a graduate with a better transcript, and the CHES coursework assumes you have seen a programme run.

programs.note: The named route — 8 Florida public institutions, all universities, 1,208 credentials with ⚠ 579 master's against 560 bachelor's. USF 423, Florida State 279, UF 198, FIU 126. ⚠⚠ Read its degrees note on why the undergraduate teaching is numbered HSC rather than PHC.

⚠⚠⚠ The comparison to make before committing, because the two overlap at the policy end and are NOT equally reachable: 24 institutions against 8, with 20 state colleges carrying the upper-division coursework against none here. ⚠ And the target occupation pays $123,860 against health education's $64,070.

⚠ Both fields live on health data and students confuse them. HIM owns the individual record; public health aggregates populations. ⚠⚠ HIM's credentials (RHIT, RHIA) are reachable with an associate degree from 31 institutions — a far shorter route to a recognised credential if that is what you want.

⚠ A real overlap rather than a neighbour: community nutrition IS public health practice, and WIC and SNAP-Ed are shared employers. ⚠⚠ The difference worth weighing is that the dietitian credential is LICENSED in Florida and health education is not licensed at all.

⚠ Not a route in, but public health nursing is a substantial destination and it fixes this path's weakest point — a public health bachelor's alone is a thin credential, and a nursing licence underneath an MPH is not. ⚠⚠ Nursing is taught at 78 Florida institutions against public health's 8.

courses.reason: ⚠⚠ Epidemiology — 9 institutions and the most widely carried undergraduate public health course in Florida. ⚠ Five of the nine are STATE COLLEGES (Eastern Florida, Palm Beach, Santa Fe, State College of Florida, Valencia), which is the only part of this field a state college reliably offers.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Florida also numbers applied epidemiology at PHC4024 (4 carriers) and community health and epidemiology at HSC3201 (4). Register by number and expect to send a syllabus on transfer.

courses.reason: Public Health Research — 7 institutions. Study design, measurement and the difference between an association and a finding; the course that makes the rest of the field legible.
Foundations of Public Health — 5 institutions. The upper-division survey: the ten essential services, the core disciplines, and how the American system is actually organised.

Introduction to Public Health — 5 institutions, and lower division, so it is the way in for a student still at the A.A. stage. ⚠ One of only three undergraduate PHC numbers with four or more carriers.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ Of the 18 PHC courses carried by four or more Florida institutions, 14 are GRADUATE. Do not judge the prefix's undergraduate offering by what the PHC catalogue looks like.

courses.reason: Overview of Public Health Programs and Policy — 4 institutions. Programme planning and policy, which is squarely inside CHES's process-course category.

⚠ Communication Theory and Practice for Health — 5 institutions. Health communication is one of NCHEC's Nine Areas and a process course, so it counts toward the 12-credit minimum rather than the capped topic allowance.
Principles of Applied Epidemiology — 4 institutions. The applied treatment: outbreak investigation, surveillance and field methods rather than theory.
Community Health and Epidemiology — 4 institutions. Combines the two halves, and several programmes use it in place of a separate epidemiology course.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Check whether your programme treats this as equivalent to HSC4500; some do and some require both.

courses.reason: Personal Health — 14 institutions, the most widely carried HSC course at lower division. A general-education entry point, and a cheap way to test whether the subject interests you.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Also numbered HSC1100 Personal and Community Health at 9 institutions. The two are close but not identical; the 1100 version carries the community half.

courses.reason: ⚠⚠ Elementary Statistics — 39 institutions. Non-negotiable on this path. Epidemiology is applied statistics, and every graduate programme assumes it.
General Sociology — 29 institutions. Public health's explanatory framework is social rather than clinical, and this is where that starts.
Introduction to Psychology — 33 institutions. Health behaviour theory — the models programme planning is built on — comes from here.
Anatomy and Physiology I — 20 institutions. ⚠ Not universally required for a public health bachelor's, but graduate programmes and employers assume you can read clinical material.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Two equivalent packagings: BSC2085 plus BSC2085L at 20 institutions, combined BSC2085C at 7.

courses.reason: Microbiology — 16 institutions. Infectious disease epidemiology is a large part of the field and it assumes you know what an organism does.
Medical Terminology — 6 institutions at upper division. Useful specifically because public health people spend their careers in rooms with clinicians who do not explain themselves.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Also numbered HSC1531 at 16 institutions and HSC2531 at 8, both lower division and cheaper.

courses.reason: English Composition I — 39 institutions. Public health is funded by grant writing and answerable to public bodies; writing is not a soft skill here.

sources.label: O*NET — Health Education Specialists (21-1091.00)
sources.note: 71,800 employed (2024), growth faster than average (5% to 6%), 7,900 annual openings, median $64,070 (2025). ⚠⚠ Education distribution: 62% associate degree, 31% bachelor's, 3% high school — which DISAGREES with BLS, and the page quotes both. Tasks include preparing health education materials, developing programmes and workshops, collaborating to determine community health needs, and designing evaluations of programme performance.

sources.label: BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook — Health Education Specialists and Community Health Workers
sources.note: ⚠⚠ BLS gives typical entry-level education as a BACHELOR'S DEGREE for health education specialists and a HIGH SCHOOL DIPLOMA for community health workers. Employment projected to grow 6 percent from 2025 to 2035, faster than average, about 6,900 openings a year. Median pay $64,070 and $51,850. ⚠ The projection decade differs from O*NET's (2025–35 against 2024–34), which accounts for part of the numeric gap; the education disagreement it does not.

sources.label: O*NET — Epidemiologists (19-1041.00)
sources.note: ⚠⚠⚠ The occupation students picture, and its size is the finding: 12,300 employed nationally, about 800 annual openings, median $87,220 (2025), growth much faster than average (7% or higher). ⚠ Education 67% master's, 22% post-doctoral training, 11% doctoral — there is effectively no undergraduate entry.

sources.label: O*NET — Community Health Workers (21-1094.00)
sources.note: 65,100 employed, growth much faster than average (7% or higher), 7,800 annual openings, median $51,850 (2025). Education 56% bachelor's, 18% associate, 13% postbaccalaureate certificate — though BLS gives typical entry as a high school diploma. ⚠ Together with health education specialists this is where the volume of public health employment actually is.

sources.label: NCHEC — CHES examination eligibility
sources.note: ⚠⚠⚠ The countable credential. A bachelor's, master's or doctoral degree from an accredited institution, PLUS either a transcript showing a major in health education OR at least 25 semester credits of coursework at C or better addressing the Nine Areas of Responsibility. ⚠⚠ Distribution: minimum 12 credits from process courses, maximum 9 from topic-focused courses, maximum 6 from other courses. ⚠ The major is NOT required — which is what makes this plannable from the first term.

Every carrier is a university: USF 423, Florida State 279, UF 198, FIU 126, UWF 80, FGCU 43. Community health and preventive medicine (51.2208): 8 institutions, 268, overwhelmingly UF. ⚠ The master's outnumbering the bachelor's happens in no other programme on this site.
